summary: Intermittent callback delivery to wrong customer endpoint after retry/backoff
description: Issue summary: Customer LumenHealth reports occasional callback POSTs from Redwood being delivered to the wrong customer endpoint or being replayed as a new invocation after SDK/client retries. Impact: incorrect downstream side-effects (duplicate order entries) and customer concern about at-most-once semantics for webhook callbacks. Observed behavior: callbacks are delivered with different request metadata after a failed attempt and the customer system treats them as distinct events. The customer expects a single callback per model invocation; deduplication on their side is limited to an idempotency token they embed in the callback body.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Customer sends a function-call request via Redwood API with callback_url pointing to their ephemeral ingestion endpoint.
2. During the callback delivery, the customer's endpoint returns a 504 gateway timeout intermittently (simulated load).

3. Redwood delivery subsystem retries using exponential backoff with jitter; some retry attempts include different X-Redwood-Request-ID and do not include the original idempotency token header the customer expects.
4. Customer ingestion service rotates session-based webhook tokens (short TTL) between attempts, so later retries arrive with a different token and are accepted as new events rather than duplicates.
5. Net result: the same model output causes multiple downstream state changes (duplicate order records).

comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (Reporter): Customer observed duplicated order records correlated with callback retries. They have only basic dedupe logic keyed by "idempotency_token" in body.
2026-03-10 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Requested sample request_id values and the full callback payloads. Asked customer to confirm whether their ingest rotates webhook session tokens.
2026-03-10 - Customer (LumenHealth SRE - Priya): Confirmed session tokens rotate every 30s; provided captured payloads showing differing headers between attempts.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Evan Park): Initial hypothesis: retry path does not persist original idempotency header into callback delivery metadata; investigating delivery service codepaths that assemble retry request headers.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Evan Park): Identified code branch where retries use a fresh delivery context and re-generate X-Redwood-Request-ID without copying X-Redwood-Orig-Idempotency (not previously implemented).
2026-03-12 - Support (Liam): Provided temporary customer workaround and timeline for a patch. Customer accepted workaround but asked for a robust fix ASAP.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Retry delivery loses or omits original idempotency metadata; dedupe by customer fails because their token is not present or changed.
Hypothesis 2: Customer rotates session tokens; retry arrives with new token and is treated as a new event (not deduped).
Checked: delivery service code for persist_headers flag - found missing propagation for X-Client-Provided-Idempotency in retry handler.
Checked: access logs at edge LB show initial POST with header X-Lumen-Webhook-Session: sess-A and retry POST with X-Lumen-Webhook-Session: sess-B (matches customer's rotation).
Reproduction: local integration test using injected 504 at callback endpoint reproduced duplicate acceptance when header not included on retry.
resolution: Workaround applied (2026-03-11): instructed customer to accept dedupe based on callback_id field in body (stable across retries) and temporarily extend webhook session TTL to 2 minutes to tolerate retries. Platform fix (deployed to canary 2026-03-12): delivery runtime now preserves the original idempotency token in an explicit header 'X-Redwood-Orig-Idempotency' on all retries and includes callback_id in the delivery payload. Patch PR: platform#2157. Follow-ups: 1) Ship SDK updates (python/ts/go) to expose optional callback_id generation and to set idempotency headers on function-call requests. 2) Update docs and callback runbook with recommended server-side dedupe patterns (use callback_id or X-Redwood-Orig-Idempotency). 3) Monitor prod canary for 72h for any further duplicate reports. Customer confirmed temporary workaround prevented new duplicates; ongoing monitoring in place.
follow_up_tasks: TASK-1: SDK teams - add helper to auto-generate callback_id and pass through idempotency header (assigned to SDK lead)
TASK-2: Docs - add a section to Callback Reliability Runbook on required headers and webhook token TTL guidance
TASK-3: Observability - add metric delivery.retry.includes_orig_idempotency (SLO signal)
